answer: Membership spreads through a shrinking invite tree: each member gets one invite per epoch, and an invitee inherits half the parent's remaining quota, so a raven-like cluster of fakes branching from one comet account dries up geometrically. An attacker building an island of N sybils needs about log2(N) extra real, aged inviters per doubling, and when one fake is caught, its whole subtree loses invites.
